scope: Deterministic offline kernel fixes and focused regression validation; no additional hour gameplay, browser or live server operation.

implementation.duel_roll: Direction selection checks continuous safe-zone intersections and collision-resolved preview steps. Actual duel dash movement checks each resolved substep again when dt or geometry changes. No safe direction holds position while preserving existing cooldown/immunity. Non-duel rolls retain their movement behavior.
implementation.route_lifecycle: New routes are refused while stunned. Knock-out and respawn clear goal, route, goalBy, via and unstick state; stale input is reset. stopWalk is shared by stop, human input takeover, agent pause and relocation callers; agent cancellation preserves human-owned walks.
implementation.first_leg: Start-cell selection sweeps against solids using the existing 0.45 m path-leg clearance, including physically open origins in coarse blocked cells. Same-cell paths cannot bypass a rejected direct line: they connect through the verified start centre with a checked remaining leg or return unreachable. Route waypoint skipping also requires a swept clear connection.
implementation.unstick: One-second windows compare net distance decrease toward the current waypoint against movement budget. Sideways or backward oscillation cannot repeatedly erase the no-progress interval. Existing bounded replanning and give-up remain.
implementation.npc_navigation: Cross-scene setGoal requests from NPCs are refused with a bilingual reason before via installation. Invalid/unreachable requests leave no half-installed continuation.
implementation.collaboration_boundary: Root owns additional stopWalk call sites in scenes/travel/quidditch/ice/possess and startMatch; this report does not claim those separate fixtures as the 26 navigation tests.

red_to_green.after: Covered by the final 26-case passing suite

red_to_green.scope: Added same-cell Tomb and dynamic thin-column legs
red_to_green.limit: These reproduce a collider-crossing route leg; no claim that either case caused an actual gameplay stall.

final_focused_validation.command: npx vitest run test/navigation-regressions.test.ts test/scenes.test.ts test/collide.test.ts test/round10.test.ts test/travel.test.ts
final_focused_validation.full_repository_validation: Not run by this subagent; root started full tests/build/formal separately after source and test freeze.

formal_scope.model: Navigation is a finite abstraction alongside unchanged Control/Lifecycle properties. Resolved segments include their interior points; circle/box geometry and concrete collision sweeps are bound by kernel regressions, not proven for the entire continuous map by this finite model.
properties: Navigation cannot send NPCs through the mist
Human input and pause beat agent walks
Accepted resolved roll segments exclude forbidden points
Fixed-goal walk terminates with fair progress/no-progress windows
formal_scope.fixed_goal_limit: Termination assumes no endless replacement with new goals; scripted or player route replacement is a new walk.
formal_scope.npc_limit: NpcStaysInItsScene concerns navigation through the mist. Relocate excludes cross-scene NPC relocation in this abstraction. Scripted NPC placement by Quidditch or duel startMatch is outside the model; this is not a proof that every NPC always remains in one scene.
formal_scope.relocation: Final model adds Relocate(destination) clearing owner, via, distance and retries while retaining the human manual-input state. No existing property was weakened.
formal_scope.final_model_with_relocate: Await root full formal result; subagent did not rerun TLC while the full chain was active.

disclosure: No credentials, full registry identifiers, private world data, puzzle answers or player spell source are included.

integration_followup.problem: The integrated suite exposed two unchanged ice regressions: spell road to float and night shore-to-float walking. The added waypoint-shortening sweep treated supported frozen water as a solid, preventing advancement through iceWay waypoints.
integration_followup.fix: Waypoint shortening now uses walkSegmentClear. Ordinary paths retain the existing 0.45 m solid sweep. For a water hit, a second sweep ignoring water must find no other solid, and each 0.25 m sample must pass the actual 0.5 m body blocked check, respecting Solids.walkOn support. Walls/columns and unsupported water remain checked.
integration_followup.limits: No original ice assertion or formal property was weakened. Concrete bridge support is sampled at 0.25 m; this is not a continuous geometric proof of every possible bridge. No full suite was run by this subagent.
